Full Instructions improve accuracy and interception and increase the selectivity of the response to events (transitions followed more than oddballs). Partial Instructions do not differ from None on most measures. Full Instructions also make the colour-cue offset more likely to be learned and applied.
Responses to events and questionnaire scores (RQ2).

Higher scores on the five questionnaires, and on their general factor, go with split placements at t+2 after transitions (nets on both the old and the new direction), fewer transitions followed at t+1 and lower selectivity at t+1. Following oddballs and overall accuracy are not associated with the scores. The split association is largest with Full Instructions. Among the subscales, it is carried by STICSA cognitive, OCI obsessing and IUS inhibitory, and not by OCI ordering and washing or IUS prospective. It remains when the replayed state uncertainty of the model is included as a covariate.

Behaviour is best described by the latent-state model. None of its six parameters is associated with the questionnaire scores or the general factor. The relative fit of latent-state and single-state models is not associated with the scores. In the hybrid switch model, 79 of 86 participants switch from tracking to latent-state inference, mostly in the second episode (median 12 trials after the first transition with None, about 7.5 with Partial and Full; not tested); switch time and reliance are not associated with the general factor.
